name: Holden
overview: General Motors-Holden (GM-H) was Australia's definitive domestic automaker and cultural icon. Emerging from an Adelaide saddlery founded by James Alexander Holden in 1856 and later coachbuilding giant Holden's Motor Body Builders (HMBB), Holden partnered with General Motors in 1931 and launched Australia's first mass-produced domestic motor vehicle, the 48-215 (popularly FX), on 29 November 1948. For seven decades, Holden engineered and manufactured vehicles tailored specifically to Australia's vast distances, harsh corrugated roads, and extreme climates at primary assembly complexes in Fishermans Bend and Dandenong (Victoria), Elizabeth and Woodville (South Australia), Pagewood (New South Wales), Acacia Ridge (Queensland), and Mosman Park (Western Australia). From the ubiquitous Kingswood, Monaro, and Torana to the legendary Commodore and luxury Statesman/Caprice, Holden shaped the Australian national identity, dominated Australian motorsport including multiple Bathurst 1000 victories, and exported vehicles across North America, the Middle East, South Africa, and New Zealand before local manufacturing ceased at Elizabeth on 20 October 2017 and the brand retired in 2020.
australian_history:
Holden's origins trace to 1856 when English immigrant James Alexander Holden established J.A. Holden & Co., a saddlery and leather goods business in Adelaide, South Australia. By 1917, under grandson Edward Wheewall Holden, wartime chassis import restrictions spurred the founding of Holden's Motor Body Builders Ltd (HMBB), which quickly became the Southern Hemisphere's largest coachbuilder, supplying bodies for GM, Ford, Chrysler, and Studebaker. In 1931, General Motors acquired HMBB to form General Motors-Holden's Ltd (GM-H). Under wartime Prime Minister Ben Chifley's post-WWII call for an Australian-built car, GM-H embarked on 'Project 2000' led by Laurence Hartnett. On 29 November 1948, Chifley famously unveiled the Holden 48-215 (later known as the FX) with the immortal words: 'She's a beauty!'.

Throughout the 1950s and 1960s, Holden held over 50% market share with the FJ (1953), the modern FE and FC series, and the breakthrough 1963 EH Holden, which introduced the ultra-reliable Red motor (149ci and 179ci) and sold over 250,000 units in 18 months. In 1968, Holden introduced the full-size HK series, introducing the iconic Kingswood nameplate, the pillarless Monaro sports coupe (which won the 1968 Bathurst 500 on debut with Bruce McPhee), and Holden's first locally designed and manufactured V8 engines (the 253ci and 308ci Red V8s cast at Fishermans Bend). The compact HB/LC/LJ Torana line cemented Holden's racing pedigree through Peter Brock and the Holden Dealer Team (HDT), achieving legendary status with the triple-carburettor LJ GTR XU-1 and the V8-powered LH/LX SL/R 5000 and A9X options.

In 1977, Holden pioneered Radial Tuned Suspension (RTS), transforming Australian handling dynamics across the HZ and Torana lineups. The oil crises of the 1970s prompted Holden to downsize from the traditional full-size Kingswood platform to a European-derived mid-size architecture, resulting in the launch of the VB Commodore in October 1978. Based on an Opel Rekord/Senator foundation but comprehensively re-engineered with 35% heavier body stiffening and rugged Australian suspension, the Commodore went on to become Australia's best-selling car for 15 consecutive years (1996-2010). Under the Australian Federal Government's Button Car Plan in the late 1980s, GM-H formed the United Australian Automobile Industries (UAAI) joint venture with Toyota, producing badge-engineered models including the Nova (Corolla) and Apollo (Camry) until 1996.

In 2006, Holden achieved its engineering pinnacle with the VE Commodore, a $1.03 billion ground-up Australian development on GM's global rear-wheel-drive Zeta platform. The Zeta platform also spawned the long-wheelbase WM Statesman/Caprice and underpinned exported vehicles including the Pontiac G8, Chevrolet SS, and Chevrolet Caprice Police Pursuit Vehicle (PPV) in the United States. Following the global financial crisis, shifting consumer preferences toward compact SUVs, the soaring Australian dollar, and escalating manufacturing cost pressures, General Motors announced in December 2013 that it would cease manufacturing in Australia. On 20 October 2017, the final Australian-built Holden—a Red Hot VF Series II Commodore SS-V Redline sedan—rolled off the Elizabeth assembly line in South Australia. Holden transitioned briefly to an all-import lineup, including the European Opel-sourced ZB Commodore and US-sourced Acadia and Equinox SUVs, before General Motors retired the historic Holden marque permanently at the end of 2020.

models_catalog.name: Holden 48-215 (FX)
models_catalog.overview: The original 'Australia's Own Car', an aerodynamically styled unibody sedan powered by the rugged 132.5ci 'Grey Motor' inline-six. In 1951, the 50-2106 coupe utility was introduced.

generations.summary: First Australian-manufactured mass-market automobile. Introduced unibody construction, 60 bhp 2.15L Grey inline-six, and 3-speed manual column shift.

models_catalog.name: Holden FJ
models_catalog.overview: The iconic face of 1950s Australia, featuring a bold horizontal chrome front grille, upgraded trim levels including the Special, and introducing the famous Panel Van.

generations.summary: Substantial facelift of the 48-215 with Standard, Business, and Special trim levels. Over 169,969 units produced.

models_catalog.name: Holden FE
models_catalog.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
models_catalog.overview: First major redesign with contemporary low-line styling, curved one-piece windscreen, 12-volt electrical system, and the introduction of the first Holden Station Sedan (wagon).

generations.summary: Modernized chassis, longer 105-inch wheelbase, 70 bhp Grey motor, pendant pedals, and first factory Holden station wagon.

models_catalog.name: Holden FC
models_catalog.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
models_catalog.overview: Facelifted FE featuring bolder grille, tail-fin chrome spears, upgraded interior, and improved 72 bhp Grey engine. Captured over 50% of the Australian passenger vehicle market.

generations.summary: High-water mark for market dominance with 191,724 units produced. Available in Standard, Business, and Special.

models_catalog.name: Holden FB
models_catalog.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
models_catalog.overview: American-inspired styling with wraparound dogleg windscreen, rear finettes, and increased interior room. The first Holden exported in left-hand drive.

generations.summary: Bigger, heavier body with 138ci Grey motor, lower center of gravity, and American 1950s styling cues.

models_catalog.name: Holden EK
models_catalog.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
models_catalog.overview: The first Holden to offer an automatic transmission—the 3-speed GM Hydra-Matic imported from the United States. Also introduced electric windscreen wipers.

generations.summary: Refined FB with Hydra-Matic 3-speed automatic option, modified rear quarter side trim, and final evolution of the 138 Grey motor.

models_catalog.name: Holden EJ
models_catalog.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
models_catalog.overview: Clean modern European-influenced styling that shed fins and wraparound glass. Introduced the ultra-luxurious Premier badge with leather upholstery and standard Hydra-Matic.

generations.summary: All-new crisp body design, Duo-Servo brakes, Premier trim with bucket seats and metallic paint, and the 1,000,000th Holden produced.

models_catalog.name: Holden EH
models_catalog.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
models_catalog.overview: One of the most beloved Holdens in history, introducing the revolutionary overhead-valve 'Red' six-cylinder engines (149ci and 179ci) with seven-bearing crankshafts.

generations.summary: Debut of the 149 and 179 Red engines, new square roofline, S4 racing homologation special, and record 256,959 units sold in 18 months.

models_catalog.name: Holden HD
models_catalog.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
models_catalog.overview: Wider, longer body featuring distinctive kidney-grille front styling and sharp front fender extensions. Introduced the twin-carburettor X2 high-performance engine option.

generations.summary: Power disc brakes option, 179 X2 twin-carb engine (140 bhp), Powerglide 2-speed automatic, and spacious new cabin.

models_catalog.name: Holden HR
models_catalog.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Ute / Panel Van
models_catalog.overview: Clever restyle of the HD with smoothed front fenders and vertical tail lamps. Introduced enlarged 161ci and 186ci Red engines, wider wheel track, and standard seatbelt anchorages.

generations.summary: Introduction of 161 and 186 Red engines, 186 X2, and 186S with twin-barrel Carter carburettor; 4-speed manual gearbox option.

models_catalog.name: Holden Kingswood / Belmont / Premier
models_catalog.vehicle_type: Sedan / Wagon / Utility / Panel Van / Cab Chassis
models_catalog.overview: The backbone of Australian family and commercial transport through the HK, HT, HG, HQ, HJ, HX, HZ, and WB series, establishing the Kingswood as an Australian cultural idiom.

generations.summary: Introduced Belmont, Kingswood, and Premier badges, energy-absorbing steering column, and Chevrolet 307 V8.
First Australian-designed Holden V8 engines (253 and 308ci Red V8s), neoprene rubber suspension bushings, and plastic grille.
Introduction of the Australian-designed Tri-Matic 3-speed automatic transmission.
Total ground-up redesign with perimeter subframe, all-coil suspension, flow-through ventilation. Best-selling single Holden series with 485,650 units built.
Squarer frontal design, wrap-around lights, Sandman surf-culture van and ute packs, improved seating and sound deadening.
Updated engines engineered to meet strict ADR 27A emission regulations; distinctive Kingswood 50th Anniversary edition.
Standardization of Radial Tuned Suspension (RTS) with four-wheel disc brakes on upper trims, revolutionizing road handling.
Commercial-only evolution featuring modern squared front clip, Blue six/V8 engines, and revised instrument panel.

models_catalog.name: Holden Monaro
models_catalog.overview: Australia's premier muscle car and two-door sports coupe, immortalized at Mount Panorama with back-to-back Bathurst victories and resurrected in 2001 as a modern grand tourer.

generations.summary: Iconic pillarless coupe styling; GTS 327 (1968 Bathurst winner) and GTS 350 (1969 Bathurst winner) powered by imported Chevrolet small-blocks.
Bold American muscle proportions, 350 V8 in HQ, 4-door GTS sedan introduced in 1973, and the collector-grade HX LE coupe.
Mike Simcoe-designed concept made reality. Powered by 5.7L LS1 V8 and supercharged V6; exported to the US as the Pontiac GTO and the UK as Vauxhall Monaro.

models_catalog.name: Holden Torana
models_catalog.overview: From Vauxhall Viva origins to triple-carburettor Bathurst champion and thunderous V8 hatchback, the Torana was central to Australian motorsport folklore.

generations.summary: Vauxhall Viva HB derived compact car with 1.2L engine, later expanded into 4-door Brabham special.
Stretched wheelbase packaging the 6-cylinder Red engine; legendary GTR and GTR XU-1 (Brock 1972 Bathurst victory with triple Stromberg 202ci).
First Australian car engineered to accommodate 4-, 6-, and 8-cylinder engines. Home to the SL/R 5000, L34, and Bathurst-conquering A9X option.
Refined front and rear styling, standard RTS suspension, Starfire 1.9L and 2.85/3.3L sixes.

models_catalog.name: Holden Statesman / Caprice
models_catalog.overview: Holden's flagship long-wheelbase luxury sedan, serving prime ministers, business leaders, and private hire fleets with cavernous rear legroom and V8 power.

generations.summary: Extended 114-inch wheelbase luxury cruiser. Statesman Custom, de Ville, and Caprice trims with 308ci V8 and plush velour/leather.
Reborn on extended VN/VP architecture with independent rear suspension (IRS), 3.8L V6, 5.0L EFI V8, and Series III supercharged V6.
Modernized styling with 5.7L LS1 V8, dual-zone climate, memory seating; exported to Middle East as Chevrolet Caprice and China as Buick Royaum.
Billion-dollar Zeta platform limousine with 6.0L L98/L77 and 6.2L LS3 V8. Supplied to the US as the Chevrolet Caprice PPV police interceptor.

models_catalog.name: Holden Commodore / Calais / Berlina
models_catalog.overview: The undisputed king of the Australian road for nearly three decades, spanning 16 series codes from the European-derived VB to the home-grown Zeta-platform VE/VF and imported ZB.

generations.generation_name: First Generation (VB, VC, VH, VK, VL)
generations.summary: Downsized family car adapted from Opel Rekord/Senator with heavy-duty Australian reinforcement; featured Red/Blue/Black sixes and Nissan RB30E/Turbo six.
Widened body designed for Australian family widths; introduction of Buick-sourced 3.8L V6, local 5.0L EFI V8, VG ute, and VR/VS IRS & driver airbags.
Smooth aerodynamic styling; all-round IRS, Gen III LS1 5.7L V8, introduction of Alloytec 3.6L V6 in VZ; spawned Monaro, Adventra, and Crewman.
Australia's $1 billion ground-up Zeta platform masterpiece. 5-star ANCAP, SIDI V6, 6.0L/6.2L V8 engines, Head-Up Display; exported as Pontiac G8 and Chevy SS.
Imported from Opel in Ruesselsheim, Germany (Insignia-based). FWD/AWD layout with 2.0L Turbo and 3.6L V6; final vehicle to carry the Commodore nameplate.

models_catalog.name: Holden Gemini
models_catalog.overview: Holden's smash-hit small car based on GM's T-Car platform and Isuzu mechanicals, winning Wheels Car of the Year in 1975 and dominating the economy market.

generations.generation_name: RWD Gemini (TX, TC, TD, TE, TF, TG)
generations.summary: RWD architecture, Isuzu G161Z 1.6L SOHC engine, RTS handling introduced on TD, Isuzu diesel option on TE, and TG ZZ/Z sporting edition.
Front-wheel-drive generation built at Acacia Ridge; 1.5L SOHC engine; replaced by the Holden Nova.

models_catalog.name: Holden Camira
models_catalog.overview: Holden's version of GM's global J-Car platform, winning 1982 Wheels Car of the Year for its ride and packaging before being challenged by early quality control issues.

generations.summary: Front-wheel-drive Family II 1.6L and 1.8L OHC engines, Family II multipoint EFI 2.0L in JE, and five-speed manual transmission.

models_catalog.name: Holden Barina
models_catalog.overview: Holden's enduring light car, evolving from Suzuki Cultus/Swift origins to European Opel Corsa generations (SB, XC) and Korean GM Daewoo models (TK, TM).

generations.summary: Built by Suzuki in Japan. Ultra-frugal 1.3L carburettor and EFI engines; Wheels COTY winner in 1985.
European Opel Corsa B and C imports with 1.4L and 1.6L 16V engines; sporty GSi and SRi hot hatch variants.
GM Korea (Daewoo Kalos/Sonic) sourced; TM introduced 1.4L Turbo RS and MyLink touchscreen infotainment.

models_catalog.name: Holden Astra
models_catalog.overview: Spanned Nissan Pulsar rebadged versions (LB-LD built in Clayton) through highly acclaimed European Opel Astra generations (TR, TS, AH, PJ, BK/BL).

generations.summary: Locally assembled with Nissan bodyshell and Holden Family II 1.6L/1.8L engines under UAAI precursor agreements.
Beloved European hot hatches and family cars; SRi, Turbo, and 177kW OPC/VXR performance flagships.
GTC/VXR coupes followed by 2016 European Car of the Year BK hatchback with 1.4T and 1.6T engines.

models_catalog.name: Holden Colorado
models_catalog.overview: Holden's tough mid-size dual-cab and cab-chassis workhorse, replacing the Rodeo and boasting 3.5-tonne towing and potent Duramax turbo-diesel torque.

generations.summary: Built in Thailand with Isuzu partnership; 3.0L 4JJ1-TC turbo diesel and 3.6L Alloytec V6.
Global GM platform with 2.8L Duramax diesel (500Nm); heavily revised in 2016 with Holden Australian chassis dynamics tuning.

models_catalog.name: Holden Rodeo
models_catalog.overview: Holden's legendary commercial workhorse manufactured by Isuzu in Japan and Thailand across KB, TF, and RA generations.

generations.summary: Renowned for bulletproof reliability, 4WD transfer cases, and Isuzu direct-injection turbo-diesels.

models_catalog.name: Holden Captiva
models_catalog.overview: High-volume family SUV offering 5- and 7-seat configurations (Captiva 5 and Captiva 7 / MaXX) with Australian-cast Alloytec V6 and diesel powertrains.

generations.summary: GM Theta platform with 3.2L/3.0L SIDI V6, 2.0L/2.2L turbo diesel, AWD and FWD configurations.

models_catalog.name: Holden Cruze
models_catalog.overview: First imported as a compact Suzuki-based AWD (YG), then manufactured locally at Elizabeth SA from 2011 to 2016 (JG/JH), producing over 126,000 Australian units.

generations.summary: Suzuki Ignis derived light crossover with 1.5L engine and on-demand AWD.
GM Delta II platform built at Elizabeth SA. 1.8L naturally aspirated, 1.4L Turbo, 1.6L Turbo SRi, and 2.0L Turbo Diesel.

models_catalog.name: Holden Jackaroo
models_catalog.overview: Tough body-on-frame 4WD manufactured by Isuzu (Bighorn/Trooper), highly respected in the Australian Outback for off-road durability.

generations.summary: Leaf-sprung rear suspension, 2.0L/2.3L/2.6L petrol and 2.2L/2.8L turbo-diesel engines.
Coil-sprung chassis, 3.2L/3.5L DOHC V6, 3.0L common-rail 4JX1-TC turbo diesel, Monterey luxury pack.

models_catalog.name: Holden Frontera
models_catalog.overview: Sporty lifestyle 4WD based on the Isuzu MU / Amigo / Rodeo platform, available in SWB Sport and LWB family variants.

generations.summary: 2.0L/2.2L 4-cylinder and 3.2L DOHC V6 with dual-range shift-on-the-fly 4WD.

models_catalog.name: Holden Adventra
models_catalog.overview: Cross-over all-wheel-drive wagon based on the VY II/VZ Commodore wagon with Cross Trac permanent AWD (62% rear torque bias) and raised ride height.

generations.summary: Cross Trac AWD with automatic brake differential; 5.7L LS1 V8 (CX8, LX8) and 190kW Alloytec V6 (CX6, LX6).

models_catalog.name: Holden Crewman
models_catalog.overview: Australian-designed and built 4-door dual-cab ute built on the extended long-wheelbase Statesman chassis, offered in RWD and Cross Trac AWD (Cross 6 / Cross 8).

generations.summary: Heavy-duty leaf-sprung rear axle, seating for five, Cross Trac AWD option, and SS 5.7L/6.0L V8 models.

models_catalog.name: Holden Vectra
models_catalog.overview: European-designed mid-size car imported initially from Belgium then manufactured locally at Elizabeth SA (1998-2001) before reverting to German imports (ZC).

generations.summary: Elizabeth-built European mid-sizer with 2.0L Family II 16V and 2.5L 24V DOHC V6.
Opel Vectra C import featuring 2.2L direct injection and 3.2L V6.

models_catalog.name: Holden Nova
models_catalog.overview: Badge-engineered Toyota Corolla built alongside the Corolla under the UAAI joint venture at Altona and Dandenong, Victoria.

generations.summary: Toyota 4A-FE 1.6L and 7A-FE 1.8L twin-cam 16-valve engines; SL, SLX, and sporty GS trims.

models_catalog.name: Holden Apollo
models_catalog.overview: Badge-engineered Toyota Camry built in Victoria under the UAAI joint venture, offering outstanding reliability with Holden branding.

generations.generation_name: Apollo JK, JL, JM, JP Series
generations.summary: Toyota 2.0L 3S-FE, 2.2L 5S-FE, and silky smooth 3.0L 3VZ-FE quad-cam V6.

models_catalog.name: Holden Calibra
models_catalog.overview: Stunning aerodynamic coupe with a drag coefficient of just 0.26 Cd, offering 2.0L 16V, 2.5L V6, and 2.0L Turbo 4x4 options.

generations.summary: Imported from Opel in Germany; 2.0L C20XE (110kW), 2.5L V6 (125kW), and 150kW C20LET Turbo 4x4 with 6-speed manual.

models_catalog.name: Holden Trax
models_catalog.overview: Popular city-sized compact crossover SUV built on GM's Gamma II platform, powered by 1.8L and 1.4L Turbo petrol engines.

generations.summary: LS, LT, and LTZ models; Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, turbo boost, and 5-star ANCAP safety.

models_catalog.name: Holden Equinox
models_catalog.overview: Mid-size American crossover imported from GM Mexico, featuring potent 188kW 2.0L Turbo and 9-speed automatic transmission.

generations.summary: 1.5L Turbo, 1.6L Turbo Diesel, and class-leading 188kW 2.0L Turbo with AWD.

models_catalog.name: Holden Acadia
models_catalog.overview: US-built full-size 7-seat family SUV (GMC Acadia twin) re-tuned by Holden engineers at Lang Lang Proving Ground for Australian conditions.

generations.summary: 3.6L V6 (231kW/367Nm), 9-speed automatic, 360-degree camera, traffic sign recognition, LT, LTZ, LTZ-V.

models_catalog.name: Holden Trailblazer / Colorado 7
models_catalog.overview: Rugged ladder-chassis 7-seat 4WD SUV based on the Colorado ute platform with 5-link coil rear suspension and 3.0-tonne towing.

generations.summary: Rebranded Trailblazer in 2016 with major interior and NVH overhaul, 2.8L Duramax diesel (147kW/500Nm).

models_catalog.name: Holden Volt
models_catalog.overview: Ground-breaking extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) capable of up to 60km of pure EV driving backed by a 1.4L petrol generator.

generations.summary: 16 kWh lithium-ion battery, 111kW drive motor, 370Nm instant torque, futuristic touch-capacitive dashboard.

models_catalog.name: Holden Spark / Barina Spark
models_catalog.overview: Youthful 5-door city microcar built in South Korea, boasting sharp styling, Apple CarPlay, and nimble handling.

generations.summary: 1.2L and 1.4L petrol engines, CVT and manual transmissions, Australian-tuned electric power steering.

models_catalog.name: Holden Cascada
models_catalog.overview: Elegant European 4-seat convertible manufactured by Opel in Gliwice, Poland, featuring an insulated acoustic triple-layered fabric roof.

generations.summary: 1.6L direct-injection turbo (125kW/260Nm), HiPerStrut front suspension, Launch Edition with 20-inch alloys.

models_catalog.name: Holden Malibu
models_catalog.overview: Mid-size global GM sedan slotted between the Cruze and Commodore, powered by 2.4L petrol and 2.0L turbo-diesel engines.

generations.summary: Epsilon II platform; CD and CDX trims with 7-inch MyLink touchscreen and Camaro-inspired tail lights.

models_catalog.name: Holden Epica
models_catalog.overview: Comfortable mid-size sedan built by GM Daewoo in Bupyeong, unique for its transversally-mounted 2.0L and 2.5L inline-6 cylinder engines.

generations.summary: Transverse Porsche-engineered 2.5L inline-six petrol and later 2.0L common-rail turbo diesel with 6-speed auto.

models_catalog.name: Holden Viva
models_catalog.overview: Value-oriented small car based on the Daewoo Lacetti, offered as a budget alternative to the European-sourced AH Astra.

generations.summary: Pininfarina-styled sedan/wagon and Giugiaro-styled hatchback powered by 1.8L Family II 16V engine.

models_catalog.name: Holden Tigra
models_catalog.overview: French-assembled (Heuliez) two-seat roadster featuring an electro-hydraulic retractable hardtop, based on the Opel Corsa C platform.

generations.summary: 1.8L Ecotec 4-cylinder (92kW/165Nm), 18-second folding metal roof, 5-speed manual transmission.

models_catalog.name: Holden Piazza
models_catalog.overview: Giorgetto Giugiaro-designed wedge coupe manufactured by Isuzu in Japan and sold through selected Holden dealerships.

generations.summary: 2.0L SOHC Turbo (4ZC1-T, 110kW), Lotus-tuned suspension upgrade, pop-up pod instrument controls.

models_catalog.name: Holden Suburban
models_catalog.overview: Colossal 8-seat or 9-seat American SUV converted in Mexico with a right-hand-drive dash from the Chevrolet Blazer.

generations.summary: 5.7L Vortec V8 petrol (190kW) and 6.5L Detroit Diesel V8 Turbo (145kW/597Nm), heavy-duty dual-range 4WD.

models_catalog.name: Holden Combo
models_catalog.overview: High-roof urban delivery van derived from the European Opel Corsa B and C passenger platforms.

generations.summary: 1.4L and 1.6L petrol engines with asymmetric rear barn doors and generous cargo volume.

models_catalog.name: Holden Shuttle
models_catalog.overview: Isuzu Fargo cab-over van and microbus imported to compete against the Toyota HiAce and Ford Econovan.

generations.summary: 1.8L and 2.0L petrol engines alongside 2.0L diesel; panel van and window van configurations.

models_catalog.name: Holden Drover
models_catalog.overview: Rebadged Suzuki Sierra (SJ413) sold through Holden dealers to fill the compact four-wheel drive niche.

generations.summary: 1.3L 4-cylinder engine, leaf springs, dual-range 4WD; highly agile in rugged terrain.

models_catalog.name: Holden Scurry
models_catalog.overview: Rebadged Suzuki Super Carry microvan providing ultra-compact commercial delivery capability.

generations.summary: 1.0L F10A 4-cylinder engine with rear-wheel drive and cab-over configuration.

models_catalog.name: Holden Sunbird
models_catalog.overview: The 4-cylinder iteration of the Torana body, re-engineered as an economy family car following fuel price shocks.

generations.summary: Initially powered by 1.9L Opel engine, later replaced by the locally built Starfire 1.9L 4-cylinder.

models_catalog.name: Holden Brougham
models_catalog.overview: Holden's first bespoke luxury vehicle, built on the HK/HT/HG Premier body with an extended 8-inch rear overhang to challenge the Ford Fairlane.

generations.summary: Standard Chevrolet 307 V8 (HK) and Holden 308 V8 (HT/HG), brocade upholstery, Powerglide or Tri-Matic automatic.

models_catalog.name: Holden FE / FC / FB / EK
models_catalog.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Utility / Panel Van
models_catalog.overview: The second and third generation post-war Holdens represented major leaps forward in Australian automotive engineering and design. Launched in July 1956, the FE introduced a completely modern, longer, lower body with wrap-around windscreen, 12-volt electrical architecture, recirculating ball steering...

generations.summary: First clean-sheet redesign of the Holden. Introduced 12-volt electrics, wrap-around windscreen, pendant clutch and brake pedals, and the first factory Station Sedan.
Refinement of the FE with bold egg-crate grille, revised chrome fins, improved steering gear, and increased 72 bhp power output. Over 191,000 produced.
Introduced prominent American-style tailfins, panoramic wrap-around windscreen with forward-slanted 'dogleg' A-pillars, lower roofline, and an enlarged 138ci Grey motor.
Historic introduction of Holden's first automatic transmission: the 3-speed Hydra-Matic. Added electric windscreen wipers, updated side chrome, and new interior trim. 150,214 built.

models_catalog.name: Holden EJ / EH / HD / HR
models_catalog.vehicle_type: Sedan / Station Sedan / Utility / Panel Van
models_catalog.overview: The 1962-1968 era represents the golden age of 1960s Holden dominance. The July 1962 EJ introduced clean, modern European-inspired styling, the milestone 1,000,000th Holden produced, and the prestigious Premier luxury model with standard automatic, leather bucket seats, and metallic paint. In August...

generations.summary: Lower, squarer modern styling, marked the 1,000,000th Holden built, and introduced the luxurious Premier nameplate. Final application of the Grey motor.
Historic launch of the 7-bearing Red Motor (149ci & 179ci). Re-profiled roofline, square rear boot and tail lights. Fastest selling car in Australian history with 256,959 units sold.
Introduced wider body with curved side glass, kidney front fenders, front disc brakes option, Powerglide 2-speed automatic, and the twin-carburettor X2 high-performance engine.
Crisp squared styling, wider track, ball-joint front suspension, standard front disc brakes on Premier, and introduced the high-output 186S engine with twin-barrel carburettor and 4-speed manual.

models_catalog.name: Holden Sandman
models_catalog.overview: The Holden Sandman is the undisputed emblem of 1970s Australian youth and beach culture. Introduced in January 1974 on the HQ series (option package XX7 / XU3), the Sandman transformed humble commercial panel vans and utilities into vibrant, psychedelic recreational machines. Featuring bold side str...

generations.summary: Inaugural Sandman package (XX7 / XU3) on HQ and HJ. Monaro GTS dash, sports wheels, bucket seats, and optional 253ci and 308ci Red V8 engines.
Large 'SANDMAN' tailgate script on HX, followed by landmark HZ introduction of Radial Tuned Suspension (RTS), front chin spoiler, and 4-wheel disc brake option.

models_catalog.name: Holden Adventra & Crewman
models_catalog.vehicle_type: All-Wheel-Drive Cross Wagon / Dual-Cab Utility / Cab Chassis
models_catalog.overview: Developed during Holden's multi-million dollar engineering expansion under the VY/VZ Commodore program, the Adventra and Crewman represented audacious Australian engineering innovations.
